scope:
Design review of 010-site-wide-agreement-check at 53cbe03 (no diff; nothing built). One reviewer, three lenses in order: spec-compliance, security, architecture. The schema has one top-level lens and no per-finding lens field, so each finding's id prefix carries its lens: SPEC = spec-compliance, SEC = security, ARCH = architecture. READ: spec.md, plan.md, research.md, tasks.md, decisions.md of this feature; specs/009-asking-to-agree/spec.md (US-4, FR-007 to FR-018) and decisions.md (D16, D22); CONSTITUTION.md, CONTEXT.md, docs/contributing/standards/testing.md; mvp_compliance/views.py, urls.py, apps.py, models.py (1-200, 450-470), admin.py (DocumentAdmin), migrations/0001_initial.py, templates/mvp_compliance/agreement.html (the hidden next field); tests/settings.py, tests/urls*.py, tests/test_migrations.py, tests/test_views.py (outline, 1385-1398, 1830-1840, 2024-2185), tests/test_admin.py (outline, 965-990, 1305-1330), tests/conftest.py (outline); demo/settings.py, demo/urls.py, demo/views.py, demo/templates/demo/landing.html (links only); pyproject.toml (pytest options); CHANGELOG.md (Unreleased). Resolved packages: Django 6.1.1 (contrib/auth/__init__.py, contrib/auth/middleware.py, contrib/auth/backends.py, contrib/sessions/middleware.py and backends base, db, signed_cookies, conf/__init__.py, conf/global_settings.py, core/signing.py, core/handlers/wsgi.py, urls/resolvers.py, db/backends/sqlite3/schema.py) and django-mvp 0.25.1 (urls.py, views/htmx.py, config.py). PROBED by running with tests.settings and demo.settings, nothing written: settings.MEDIA_URL and STATIC_URL as Django returns them, resolve() of the page and of the sign-out addresses in both projects, reverse('landing') in the demo, importing mvp.views.htmx, json.dumps of a datetime. NOT REVIEWED: templates beyond the lines named, seed_demo, docs/*.md beyond the lines named, the admin beyond DocumentAdmin. The amendment of FS-009's FR-008, FR-012 and FR-018 was taken as approved.

Q1 (the session). 'AuthenticationMiddleware has already loaded the session' is not what the resolved code does: django/contrib/auth/middleware.py:41 sets request.user to a SimpleLazyObject and reads nothing. The session is loaded the first time something evaluates request.user, which is the check's own step 1 (auth/__init__.py:288 reads session[BACKEND_SESSION_KEY]; sessions/backends/base.py:242-255 loads on first access). For a page that reads request.user anyway, which is every page drawn in django-mvp's shell, the conclusion holds: reading one more key costs nothing. For a view that never reads it, the check adds the session read and the user read to every signed-in request, whatever is stored: SPEC-004. db backend: load is one SELECT, the write at step 4 sets modified (base.py:57-59) and SessionMiddleware saves once on that response (sessions/middleware.py:48-60, db.py:114-129, one UPDATE), and not at all on a 5xx. signed_cookies backend: load decodes the cookie with no query (signed_cookies.py:6-24) and the write is a Set-Cookie with no query (39-46); the user read is still one query on either backend. Both sides of the flush: login() for a DIFFERENT user flushes (auth/__init__.py:177-187) and logout() always flushes (241), so does a changed password hash (316). login() for the SAME user with a matching hash keeps the session and the stored finding (the branch at 178-183 is not taken), which is the same account and harmless. A session that began anonymous is not flushed at login, only given a new key with its data kept (189, and the docstring at 172-173), but the check returns at step 1 for an anonymous request and never reaches the write at step 4, so an anonymous session can hold no finding to carry over. The claim that a finding never passes between accounts holds. The value stored must be a number or a string, not a datetime: the default serializer is plain json (core/signing.py:164-165, global_settings.py:515): ARCH-001.

Q2 (the seven steps). Served when they should be stopped: (a) MEDIA_URL left unset. Django's default is '' (global_settings.py:300) and the setting is returned with the script prefix added (conf/__init__.py:220-232), so settings.MEDIA_URL is '/' in tests.settings and in demo.settings (probed). '/' is a path on this site and every address is beneath it, so the fourth bullet of 'What stays reachable' as written makes every address reachable and the check stops nobody: SPEC-002. STATIC_URL = '' or '/' does the same; STATIC_URL unset is None (global_settings.py:308) and is not prefixed. A value on another host starts with http:// or https:// and is left alone, and '//cdn.example/static/' starts with '/' and has to be told apart by parsing it. (b) An entry of the project's list of '/' covers the whole site by FR-016's own rule, and the plan's demo lists exactly that: reverse('landing') is '/' (probed): SPEC-003. An entry of '' has no segment and the plan does not say what it covers. (c) The setting given as a string and not a list: SEC-001. Redirected in a loop: (d) the page routed outside the namespace (demo/urls.py:11; probed: resolve('/legal/agree/') has app_names [] and reverse still gives '/legal/agree/') is caught by the path rule, and T006 tests it. Under a script prefix that rule works only if reverse(), which carries the prefix, is compared with request.path and not request.path_info (core/handlers/wsgi.py:61-67); the plan does not say which: SPEC-005. (e) A project's own view whose is_optional() answers true for an enforced document: the page sends the person on, the check sends them back: ARCH-002. No loop found for: the package mounted at the site root (reverse gives '/agree/', and the slug route then answers every unmatched one-segment address with the package's own 'not found', which is served and reveals nothing of the project); a path that resolves to nothing (redirected once, and after agreeing the person gets the 404); '/legal/agree' without its slash (redirected to the page with next='/legal/agree', which views.py:288-304 recognises as the page itself); signing out and then the sign-in page (anonymous at step 1); a POST to the demo's own page (reachable by path). A dot segment under STATIC_URL ('/static/../admin/') is beneath it segment by segment and matches no route, so it is a 404 and not a way through. resolve() and reverse() in __call__ read ROOT_URLCONF and not request.urlconf: note. Order itself: steps 1 to 5 put no user on the wrong side. Step 7 last means a stopped user's every request, static files included, runs the outstanding query, which the plan states.

Q3 (FR-021 against US-5 scenario 5, by D15). No scenario contradicts D15's reading. US-5 scenario 5 requires it. US-5 scenario 6, US-1 scenario 10 as T006 reads it, and SC-004 are each worded for a user with nothing enforced outstanding, who is found clear at step 4 before the permission is read. What D15 narrows is prose, not a scenario: the last sentence of FR-021 and D7's 'Deciding whether an account is let past falls under the same rule'. A permission holder with an enforced document outstanding costs the outstanding query and two permission queries on every request (auth/backends.py:174-178 caches on the user object, which lasts one request); a superuser costs none for the permission. The story's own example, a support team let past by a group, is the case that pays.

Q4 (HX-Redirect). Not verifiable against the resolved packages: no copy of htmx is installed, django-mvp 0.25.1 ships none, and django_htmx is not installed, so mvp.views.htmx itself does not import here (probed: ModuleNotFoundError). The only resolved evidence is indirect: mvp/views/htmx.py:9 and :29 answer an htmx form with HttpResponseClientRedirect, the 200-with-HX-Redirect shape. From htmx's own documentation, which I could not open here: HX-Redirect makes the browser load the given address as a whole page and is acted on before any swap, so an empty 200 body is not swapped in; a 3xx is followed by the browser inside the request, htmx never sees it or its headers, and the final 200 is swapped into the target. research.md states both correctly. Treat the two htmx statements as documented and unprobed. A link boosted by django-mvp's sidebar option (mvp/config.py:66-67) is an htmx GET for a whole page and loses its return address under D16: note.

Q5 (AgreementView.get()). US-3, 12 of 12 pass against plan.md 'The page that asks' with post() unchanged: 1, 2 (views.py:356-358 with every remaining entry optional or none); 3, 4 (a required entry remains, 200); 5 (get_entries lists everything outstanding); 6 (no required entry and next present, redirect); 7 (no next, drawn); 8 (the form's hidden next is the default destination, agreement.html:32 and views.py:383); 9 (no entries); 10 (the write is atomic, views.py:349-355); 11 (is_optional reads the field with no middleware involved); 12 (get() differs from today only when an entry is optional). FS-009 US-4, 8 of 8: 1 to 7 pass, 6 for a person with only unenforced documents now ends at the default destination without the page being drawn, and 8 is documentation. What fails is not a scenario but an existing test: tests/test_views.py:2166-2174 asserts the opposite of FR-030 and T012 forbids editing it: SPEC-001. A link that carries next no longer shows the page to a person with only unenforced documents, and the demo's own button and the documented example are such links: SPEC-006.

Q6 (migration). AddField(default=True) on a BooleanField gives every existing row True and touches no other table, and AlterModelOptions carries the permission into migration state, which is enough for FR-024 with 0001 released. The permission row itself is created by auth's post_migrate handler after migrate, not by the operation, so 'exists after migrating' holds for a real migrate. No RunPython is needed and tests/test_migrations.py:26-38 keeps passing. The planned backward-then-forward test is possible in that file but not under the marker the file uses: ARCH-003. Historical models have no publish(), so the test writes a version that satisfies the check constraint by hand, and acceptances through bulk_create as line 59 already does.

Q7 (coverage). FR against tasks: 33 of 33 traced to a task. 29 of 33 have a planned test that fails when unmet; the four without are prose or translation and need none under testing.md section 1: FR-025 (wrapping, by review and the catalog), FR-026 (docs: T003 for enforcement per document, T010, T013, T015, T017, T019), FR-027 (T005), FR-033 (T001). FR-001, 002, 003, 004, 005, 006, 007, 008, 021, 023 T006/T007; 009 T008/T009; 010, 011, 012, 013, 024 T002/T003 (013 also T004); 014 T004/T005; 015 T002 and T011; 016, 017 T014/T015; 018, 019, 020 T016/T017; 022 T018/T019; 028 to 032 T011/T012. SC against tasks: 10 of 10 (SC-001, 002, 003, 004, 010 T006; 005 T018; 006 T002; 007 T016; 008, 009 T011). Scenarios against tasks: 49 of 49 (US-1 12 of 12: 1 to 11 T006, 12 T006 and T008; US-2 10 of 10: 1 and 3 T006, 2, 4, 6, 8, 9, 10 T002, 4, 5, 6 T004, 7 T018; US-3 12 of 12 T011, 12 by the untouched suite once SPEC-001 is applied; US-4 4 of 4 T014; US-5 6 of 6 T016; US-6 5 of 5: 1, 2, 4, 5 T018, 3 T006). Thin spots inside covered items: two of the three sign-out names and the no-request.user branch have no test (SPEC-008); the second half of US-2 scenario 6, a user no longer redirected once enforcement is switched off, is shown only through T006's user whose one outstanding document is not enforced. No task lacks a requirement behind it, bar the one test in SPEC-007.

Q8 (tests). Change detector or appearance: T004 asserts list_display itself and 'the rendered cell' of a boolean column, which in the admin is an icon; and 'nothing is stored in their session' in T006 and T018 can only be written against the key's name: SPEC-007. Pass before their implementing task, all of them the must-not side of a rule and acceptable as such, but none can be shown red first: TestAgreementCheckOff (T006), 'middleware absent, neither check' and 'subclass ahead, neither' (T008), the defaults still served (T014 scenario 3), 'neither is redirected' and 'a name that matches no account' (T016), the 300-second cases (T018), scenarios 3, 9 and 10 in T011, and T004's list query count, which also duplicates tests/test_admin.py:1311. No planned test asserts wording. Query counts are compared, never pinned.

ROUTES (security lens): none added or changed in routing. The middleware answers before any view for a signed-in user it stops; next is taken from the request's own path and checked by the page (views.py:278-283); HX-Request is the user's own header and only changes the shape of the refusal. One permission is added (Document.skip_agreement, FR-019, approved in the spec). Verdict request_changes: one verified high finding, SPEC-001, a tasks.md edit.

The builder is left to choose between a red suite, editing a test the task forbids editing, or bending get() so the old test still passes, which would break FR-030 and US-3 scenario 6.

findings.claim: [spec-compliance] 'The path is beneath STATIC_URL or MEDIA_URL, when that setting is a path on this site' makes every address reachable in any project that leaves MEDIA_URL unset, which includes this repository's test settings and the demo. Built as written, the check stops nobody (FR-003, SC-002). T006's first test would catch it, and the builder would then have to invent the rule the plan leaves out; the obvious guess, skipping '' and '/', is wrong under a script prefix.
findings.evidence: .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/django/conf/global_settings.py:300 MEDIA_URL = ''; :308 STATIC_URL = None. .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/django/conf/__init__.py:220-232 adds the script prefix to either setting unless it starts with http://, https:// or '/', so '' comes back as the script prefix. Probed under tests.settings: settings.MEDIA_URL == '/', settings.STATIC_URL == '/static/'. tests/settings.py and demo/settings.py set no MEDIA_URL. plan.md:127 and research.md:96-97 give no rule for a value that is the site root, is None, or names a host without a scheme.
findings.suggested_fix: plan.md 'What stays reachable', third bullet: add 'A value covers nothing when it is None, when it is the site root (equal to get_script_prefix(), which is what Django returns for an empty setting), or when urlsplit() finds a scheme or a host in it.' tasks.md T006: say the STATIC_URL and MEDIA_URL cases set both with override_settings, and that every redirect test in the class runs with MEDIA_URL unset, which is the regression test for this. No new test.
findings.reproduction: DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=tests.settings python -c "import django; django.setup(); from django.conf import settings; print(repr(settings.MEDIA_URL))" prints '/'.

findings.claim: [spec-compliance] The demo is planned to list its landing page as reachable, and the landing page's address is '/'. By FR-016 an entry covers itself and everything beneath it, so '/' covers the whole site: from T015 on, the demo's check stops nobody, and the Independent Tests of US-1, US-2, US-4 and US-5, all run in the demo, cannot show a redirect. The plan also never says what an entry of '/' or '' covers, so a project that lists '/' to keep its home page open switches the check off without being told.
findings.evidence: plan.md:189-191 and tasks.md:56 (T015: 'demo/settings.py lists the landing page's address'). demo/urls.py:17 path('', LandingView.as_view(), name='landing'); probed under demo.settings: reverse('landing') == '/'. spec.md FR-016. plan.md:130-132 defines 'beneath' by segments and '/' has none.
findings.suggested_fix: plan.md 'The demo' and tasks.md T015: do not list the landing page. List no address in the demo's settings, and drop 'so the list of demo accounts can be read by a user who is being stopped' (a stopped user signs out, which is reachable, and reads the list signed out). plan.md 'What stays reachable': add 'An entry of / covers every address, as FR-016 has it, and an empty entry covers nothing.' T015's docs line: say that listing / switches the check off for everybody.

findings.claim: [spec-compliance] research.md's premise that AuthenticationMiddleware has already loaded the session is false for the resolved Django: it is the check's own step 1 that loads the session and the user. For a view that never reads request.user the check therefore adds two queries (db sessions) to every signed-in request, clear finding or not, which FR-021 says it must not; and it marks the session accessed on every request, anonymous ones included, so a response that carried no 'Vary: Cookie' gains one (US-1 scenario 4, 'exactly as it would be without the check'). In a django-mvp project every page draws the user menu, so the real cost is nil; the risk is T006's cost and anonymous tests being written against a view that reads nothing and failing for a reason the builder cannot remove.
findings.evidence: .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/django/contrib/auth/middleware.py:41 request.user = SimpleLazyObject(...). .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:278-300 get_user reads the session then the user row. .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:242-255 sets accessed and loads; .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py:45-47 and 80-81 add Vary: Cookie when accessed. research.md:48-50, decisions.md D14 ('the session is already loaded to find the user').
findings.suggested_fix: No design change: nothing can tell a signed-in user without reading the session. research.md 'Where nothing stops this user is remembered', first bullet and D14: say the check reads request.user, which loads the session and the user as any page that shows the user does, and that reading the key then costs nothing more. tasks.md T006: the cost tests and the anonymous test request a page that reads request.user (a document's page does, views.py:46), and the anonymous comparison is of status and redirect target. T010 docs: one sentence that a view which never touches the session now reads it.

findings.claim: [spec-compliance] The plan does not say which of request.path and request.path_info each reachability rule is compared with. They differ under a script prefix. reverse() and STATIC_URL/MEDIA_URL carry the prefix; resolve() must be given path_info, which the plan does say. If the page's own path is compared with path_info, a project that serves under a prefix and routes the page to its own view ahead of the include, as the demo does, redirects a stopped user from the page to the page for ever.
findings.evidence: plan.md:124 'the path is the path of reverse(...)' and :127-128 'the path is beneath'. .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:61-67 (path = script name + path_info). .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/django/urls/base.py:44 reverse prefixes with get_script_prefix(). demo/urls.py:11 routes the page outside the namespace (probed: app_names == []), so only the path rule keeps it reachable.
findings.suggested_fix: plan.md 'What stays reachable': add one sentence. 'The page's own path, STATIC_URL and MEDIA_URL are compared with request.path; resolve() and the project's entries use request.path_info, so an entry is written as the project's URLconf writes it.' No new test: no test in this repository runs under a prefix.

findings.claim: [spec-compliance] After T012 a link to the page that carries next no longer shows it to a person whose only outstanding documents are not enforced, and the two links the repository offers for opening the page are both of that kind. In the demo, the button 'Open the page that asks' sends such a person straight to the list of what they agreed to, so the step of US-3's Independent Test 'Open the page directly and confirm the other document is offered', and SC-009, cannot be done from the demo's own page. The documented example would teach projects the same dead link.
findings.evidence: demo/templates/demo/landing.html:63 href="{% url 'mvp_compliance:agree' %}?next={% url 'mvp_compliance:agreed' %}". docs/pages.md:220 Review our documents. plan.md:168-171 (FR-030). Neither file is named in plan.md 'The demo' or in T012 or T013.

(a) T004's list query count passes before T005, because a boolean column adds no query, and an existing test already makes the same assertion. findings.claim: [security] Both list settings fail open when a project writes a string where a list belongs. MVP_COMPLIANCE_AGREEMENT_EXEMPT_USERS = 'monitoring' lets past every account whose name is a substring of it ('mon', 'on', 'ring'), because 'in' on a string is a substring test. MVP_COMPLIANCE_AGREEMENT_EXEMPT_URLS = '/help/' is read a character at a time, and its first entry is '/', which covers the whole site. Either way the check stops fewer people than the developer believes and nothing reports it (SC-002, FR-018). Django refuses a string for its own list settings for this reason.
findings.evidence: plan.md:97 step 3 ('get_username() is in MVP_COMPLIANCE_AGREEMENT_EXEMPT_USERS') and :128. Probed: 'mon' in 'monitoring' is True; list('/help/')[0] == '/'. .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/django/conf/__init__.py (tuple_settings: ALLOWED_HOSTS, INSTALLED_APPS and others raise ImproperlyConfigured when given a string).
findings.suggested_fix: plan.md 'The system checks' and tasks.md T008/T009: one more check in the same module, mvp_compliance.E003, raised when either setting is a str, with one test case per setting. Nothing at run time.

findings.claim: [security] An account is let past by the value it signs in with, and the spec's own edge case leaves the name of a deleted account in the settings. On a site where people choose their own username, or sign in with an email they can change, whoever next takes that value is let past. The consequence is one person skipping the page, not access to anyone's data.
findings.evidence: plan.md:138-139; spec.md Edge Cases ('A user's account is named in the settings and is also deleted. The name matches nobody and nothing fails'). Not demonstrated against a registration flow: the package has none.
findings.suggested_fix: tasks.md T017, docs/enforcement.md: one sentence. 'Remove a name when its account is removed, and name only accounts whose sign-in value the account holder cannot change.' No code.

findings.claim: [architecture] Store when the finding was made, as a number, and not the time it expires. As planned: (a) 'a time' stored as a datetime raises TypeError when the session is saved, because the default serializer is plain json; (b) a project that shortens the interval keeps honouring findings stored under the old one until they expire, which FR-022's 'within a delay the project can set' does not allow for; (c) an interval of 0 needs its own rule, 'nothing stored is honoured', and T018 a test for it. Comparing now minus the stored time with the current interval removes (b) and (c) with one expression.
findings.evidence: plan.md:95-99 (steps 2 and 4) and :149-150. .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/django/core/signing.py:164-165 json.dumps with no encoder; .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/django/conf/global_settings.py:515. Probed: json.dumps of a datetime raises 'Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable'.
findings.suggested_fix: plan.md step 2: 'the session holds, under mvp_compliance_clear_since, the time the user was found clear as a POSIX timestamp, and less than the interval has passed since'. Step 4 stores timezone.now().timestamp(). 'The delay': drop 'nothing stored is honoured' as a separate rule; with 0 the comparison is never true, and step 4 still skips the write. A stored value that is not a number is treated as absent.

findings.claim: [architecture] The check asks the queryset and the page asks is_optional(), which T012 keeps as the method a project's own view overrides. FR-015 requires the page to act on the answer the check acts on. A project view that answers true for an enforced document sends a stopped person on to next, the check sends them back to the page, and the browser stops on a redirect loop. The demo did exactly this by slug until this plan removes it; any project that copied the demo's view and then adds the middleware has the loop.
findings.evidence: plan.md:166-171 and tasks.md:48 ('the method is still the one a project's own view overrides'); views.py:228-240 docstring 'A project's own view overrides this'; demo/views.py:24-33; plan.md:98 step 4 asks enforced_outstanding_for() and never the view. spec.md FR-015.
findings.suggested_fix: tasks.md T012 and T013: is_optional()'s docstring and docs/pages.md say an override may make a document that is not enforced required, and must not make an enforced one optional on a site that has switched the check on, because the check does not ask the view. CHANGELOG 'Changed' says the same for projects that overrode it. No code.

findings.claim: [architecture] The backward-then-forward migration test cannot run under the marker tests/test_migrations.py uses. The file's database tests are @pytest.mark.django_db, which wraps each in a transaction, and SQLite's schema editor refuses to run inside one. The test also leaves the schema at 0001 for every later test if it fails between the two migrations.
findings.evidence: tests/test_migrations.py:40 and :45 (django_db). .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/django/db/backends/sqlite3/schema.py:28-38 raises NotSupportedError when foreign key checks cannot be switched off, which is the case inside atomic(). tests/settings.py:61-66 is SQLite in memory. tasks.md:28 (TestEnforcedColumn).
findings.suggested_fix: tasks.md T002: TestEnforcedColumn is marked django_db(transaction=True), drives MigrationExecutor, and migrates to the leaf again in a fixture's teardown so a failure cannot leave the schema behind. The published version is written through the historical model with the fields the check constraint needs, since historical models have no publish().

notes: decisions.md D8 says django-mvp's pages make requests for parts of themselves; research.md:103-104 says django-mvp loads no htmx of its own, and mvp.views.htmx does not import in this environment (django_htmx is not installed). D8's sentence wants the research's wording.

research.md and plan.md describe htmx's handling of HX-Redirect and of a 3xx without a citation, and none is possible from the resolved packages. docs/enforcement.md should present it as htmx's documented behaviour.

D16 passes no return address for any htmx request. A link boosted by django-mvp's sidebar option (mvp/config.py:66-67) is an htmx GET for a whole page, sends HX-Boosted, and could keep its address under FR-004. Not raised as a finding: it rests on htmx behaviour that could not be verified here.
plan.md 'Requirement coverage' omits T003 for FR-026 (enforcement set per document is documented in docs/models.md by T003) and T004 for FR-013 (changed from the admin).

The settings are named EXEMPT_USERS and EXEMPT_URLS while the spec, the stories and the docs outline say 'let past' and 'kept reachable'. CONTEXT.md has neither word. Pick one pair before the names reach the README.

plan.md 'The system checks' runs both only when the exact dotted path is in MIDDLEWARE, while E002 accepts a subclass of AuthenticationMiddleware. A project's subclass of AgreementMiddleware gets neither check. The plan says the class has no hooks for subclasses, so this is consistent, and worth one sentence in the docs.
resolve() and reverse() called in __call__ read ROOT_URLCONF, not a request.urlconf set by another middleware. No project here sets one.
tasks.md T006 cites 'US-2 scenarios 1 and 3' for the user whose only outstanding document is not enforced; scenario 3 (both outstanding, the enforced one accepted) is the last case of T011.
T011's scenario 11 line cites the edge case of enforcement switched on while the page is open, but tests it switched off. One more submission with it switched on covers the edge case as written.
research.md:67-68 cites django/contrib/auth/backends.py:174 for has_perm(); 174-178 is get_all_permissions and its per-request cache, which is the point being made.

Step 4 adds a session write once per interval to requests that otherwise write nothing. With database sessions that widens Django's usual last-write-wins window for a project that also keeps its own data in the session. Standard behaviour, for docs/enforcement.md at most.
